records.evidence: 2026 conference abstract O33: ENERGIZE open-label extension NCT04770753 had 182 entrants; 121 were originally mitapivat-treated. Among 55 primary responders, mean reported hemoglobin-response duration increased from 17.9 weeks in double-blind treatment to 43.6 weeks including extension. Of 121 continuing mitapivat, 72 (59.5%) showed an open-label Hb response. Open-label post-hoc, subject to selection and no contemporaneous randomized control; not independent replication.
records.criticalLimit: Exploratory post-hoc OLE; durability observation is not independent randomized confirmation.

records.evidence: ENERGIZE-T trial NCT04770779: treatment emergent AEs 155/172 (90%) mitapivat and 71/85 (84%) placebo; serious AEs 19/172 (11%) versus 13/85 (15%); ten (6%) vs one (1%) discontinued study treatment for adverse events. Open-label long-term safety remains ongoing.
records.criticalLimit: Reported 48-week randomized safety denominators; does not prove longer term safety or FDA benefit-risk acceptance.

records.evidence: 48-week double-blind ENERGIZE-T treatment discontinuations due to adverse events were 10/172 (6%) mitapivat versus 1/85 (1%) placebo; no deaths reported. OLE endpoints pending.
records.criticalLimit: Duration 48 weeks; adverse-event causality and longer term risk not independently settled.

records.evidence: EMBARQ-CSU1 randomized Phase 3 barzolvolimab efficacy at 150 mg Q4W persisted through Week24: UAS7=0 complete response 42.4% at Week12 and 49.0% at Week24 versus placebo 9.3% and 15.4%, with sponsor-adjusted p<0.00001. Separate study CSU2 corroborates primary efficacy but long-term Week52 is not yet available.
records.criticalLimit: Issuer-filed topline; full 52-week durability and complete SAP/missing-data assessment not established.

records.evidence: EMBARQ-CSU2 randomized Phase 3 barzolvolimab 150 mg Q4W had Week12 UAS7=0 response 45.7% and Week24 54.0% versus placebo 12.6% and 17.6% (sponsor-adjusted p<0.00001). Separate CSU1 corroborates the Week12 endpoint; 52-week outcomes remain pending.
records.criticalLimit: Issuer-filed topline, not independently reanalyzed complete long-term datasets.

records.evidence: EMBARQ-CSU1 omalizumab-refractory subgroup Week12 UAS7=0: 150 mg Q4W barzolvolimab 55.3% versus 9.3% placebo, company-reported p<0.00001. No confirmed interaction p-value, subgroup multiplicity, or independent review.
records.criticalLimit: Subgroup observation, not proof of effect modification.

records.evidence: EMBARQ-CSU2 omalizumab-refractory subgroup Week12 UAS7=0: 150 mg Q4W 41.7% vs placebo 15.1%, issuer p=0.0089. Detailed interaction tests and multiplicity strategy unavailable.
records.criticalLimit: Prespecified subgroup status not independently established; not head-to-head with omalizumab.

records.evidence: Celldex 2026 Q3 SEC filing describes barzolvolimab as well tolerated to Week24 in EMBARQ-CSU1. Phase3 exact-study arm-level serious AE and discontinuation tables are not provided by this qualitative statement.
records.criticalLimit: Qualitative issuer safety characterization only; do not assign post-1-5 grade based solely on this.

records.evidence: Celldex 2026 Q3 SEC filing describes barzolvolimab as well tolerated to Week24 in EMBARQ-CSU2. No full exact-study arm-level severe events/discontinuation table is established by this statement.
records.criticalLimit: Qualitative sponsor description insufficient to grade post-1-5.

records.evidence: IZAR-1 trial NCT06641076 sponsor reports improvements in HAQ-DI and SF-36 PCS with sonelokimab in biologic-naïve psoriatic arthritis. Magnitudes, confidence intervals, and full independent comparison were not in the cited topline description.
records.criticalLimit: No arm-level numerical patient-reported effect size verified; not a new numerical grade.

records.evidence: MoonLake's IZAR-1 press release states blinded safety consistent with previous studies and no new safety signals. It does not provide complete matched serious-event and discontinuation tables for the studied dose.
records.criticalLimit: Qualitative source fact, insufficient to grade post-1-5 safety.
